# ListenerAirAbsorption <img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14">

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [3D Sound](Blitz3D-3D-Sound)

</div>


```blitzbasic
ListenerAirAbsorption:Void amount:Float32
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `amount` | In | Float32 | required | How strong it is. `0` (the default) is off. At `1` the cutoff is 20 kHz at 100 meters, 2 kHz at 1 km and 200 Hz at 10 km; `2` halves those distances. Below 0 is a runtime error. |

## Description

<img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14"> This command does not exist in the original Blitz products. BlitzLLVM adds it.

Lets distant sounds lose their high frequencies, as air does: every sound that comes from an entity gets a low-pass whose cutoff falls with its distance. This is a BlitzLLVM extension.

## Differences

* The cutoff is 2,000,000 Hz divided by the amount times the distance in meters ([ListenerDistance](ListenerDistance) sets the meters in a unit). It changes for channels that play already, too, and follows their distance like the volume does. The low-pass comes before the channel's own [effects](AddChannelEffect). [GetListenerAirAbsorption](GetListenerAirAbsorption) tells the value.

## Examples

```blitzbasic
; Thunder far away rumbles, close by it cracks.
ListenerAirAbsorption 1
```
